evidence.query: how does the water cycle maintain its operations
evidence.title: Pressurized water reactor
evidence.text: A pressurized water reactor (PWR) is a type of light-water nuclear reactor. PWRs are the most common type of nuclear power reactor, representing almost 70% of the world's commercial reactor fleet. Some countries, such as Canada and (historically) the United Kingdom, have relied heavily on other designs while others, including Japan and India, operate a mix of PWRs and other reactor types.
